Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From e111cbc4adf9f9974eed040aeece7e17460f6bff Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Emil Tantilov <emil.s.tantilov@intel.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 16:12:17 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] idpf: fix memory leak in idpf_vc_core_deinit()

Make sure to free hw->lan_regs. Reported by kmemleak during reset:

unreferenced object 0xff1b913d02a936c0 (size 96):
  comm "kworker/u258:14", pid 2174, jiffies 4294958305
  hex dump (first 32 bytes):
    00 00 00 c0 a8 ba 2d ff 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00  ......-.........
    00 00 40 08 00 00 00 00 00 00 25 b3 a8 ba 2d ff  ..@.......%...-.
  backtrace (crc 36063c4f):
    __kmalloc_noprof+0x48f/0x890
    idpf_vc_core_init+0x6ce/0x9b0 [idpf]
    idpf_vc_event_task+0x1fb/0x350 [idpf]
    process_one_work+0x226/0x6d0
    worker_thread+0x19e/0x340
    kthread+0x10f/0x250
    ret_from_fork+0x251/0x2b0
    ret_from_fork_asm+0x1a/0x30

Fixes: 6aa53e861c1a ("idpf: implement get LAN MMIO memory regions")
Signed-off-by: Emil Tantilov <emil.s.tantilov@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Aleksandr Loktionov <aleksandr.loktionov@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Joshua Hay <joshua.a.hay@intel.com>
Tested-by: Samuel Salin <Samuel.salin@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Tony Nguyen <anthony.l.nguyen@intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/idpf/idpf_virtchnl.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/idpf/idpf_virtchnl.c
index 5bbe7d9294c1..01bbd12a642a 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/idpf/idpf_virtchnl.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/idpf/idpf_virtchnl.c
@@ -3570,6 +3570,7 @@ int idpf_vc_core_init(struct idpf_adapter *adapter)
  */
 void idpf_vc_core_deinit(struct idpf_adapter *adapter)
 {
+	struct idpf_hw *hw = &adapter->hw;
 	bool remove_in_prog;
 
 	if (!test_bit(IDPF_VC_CORE_INIT, adapter->flags))
@@ -3593,6 +3594,9 @@ void idpf_vc_core_deinit(struct idpf_adapter *adapter)
 
 	idpf_vport_params_buf_rel(adapter);
 
+	kfree(hw->lan_regs);
+	hw->lan_regs = NULL;
+
 	kfree(adapter->vports);
 	adapter->vports = NULL;
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### Files Modified:
- **`drivers/net/ethernet/intel/idpf/idpf_virtchnl.c`**
  - Added a local variable `struct idpf_hw *hw = &adapter->hw;` to access the hardware structure.
  - Added `kfree(hw->lan_regs);` to free the memory allocated for LAN registers.
  - Set `hw->lan_regs = NULL;` to avoid dangling pointers after deinitialization.

### Relationships Between Modifications:
The change ensures symmetric resource management: `hw->lan_regs` is allocated in `idpf_vc_core_init()` (via `idpf_vc_core_init` calling allocation functions) but was never freed in the corresponding deinitialization function `idpf_vc_core_deinit()`. This patch adds the missing `kfree` call and resets the pointer to `NULL`, fixing a memory leak that occurred during device resets. The modification aligns with the existing pattern of freeing other allocated resources (e.g., `adapter->vports`) in the same function.

Based on your summary and the commit message in the patch, you need to:

1. analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 
2. output the file name that is most likely to cause the bug.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>
hw->lan_regs = kzalloc(sizeof(*hw->lan_regs), GFP_KERNEL);   // in idpf_vc_core_init()
</text>
<text>
// Missing in idpf_vc_core_deinit(): kfree(hw->lan_regs); hw->lan_regs = NULL;
</text>
Reason:
The allocation in `idpf_vc_core_init()` creates heap memory for `hw->lan_regs`. However, the deinitialization function `idpf_vc_core_deinit()` does not free that memory, causing it to be leaked each time the core is reinitialized (e.g., during device reset). The missing `kfree()` is the direct cause of the leak.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>
kfree(hw->lan_regs);
hw->lan_regs = NULL;
</text>
Reason:
These lines explicitly free the memory allocated for `hw->lan_regs` and set the pointer to `NULL` to prevent use-after-free. They are added at the appropriate place in `idpf_vc_core_deinit()`, ensuring proper cleanup during core deinitialization.
